newsitem.title: RUSSIA: De Beers to end Russia deal as promised.
newsitem.headline: De Beers to end Russia deal as promised.

text.p: South Africa's De Beers will make good its threat in 1997 to stop buying diamonds from Russia under an interim agreement and will buy diamonds on a "willing seller, willing buyer" basis, its Moscow representative said on Tuesday.
"From January, our formal commitment falls away," Raymond Clark, De Beers' Moscow representative, told Reuters.

"We anticipate buying diamonds from Russia, but in a different way. Assuming Russia has diamonds to sell to us, we will be a willing buyer until we get down to more formal discussions on the renewal of the trade agreement," he said.
A five-year deal between Moscow and De Beers expired in December 1995 and was replaced in February 1996 by a memorandum that acted as an interim agreement.
Clark said he could not say whether a new round of negotiations on a trade agreement would be necessary before Russia would sign a deal. "It is impossible to speculate," he said.
De Beers said earlier in December that it would no longer buy diamonds according to an interim agreement after the end of the year if Russia had not signed a draft negotiated export deal by then.
Russian diamond industry officials have for months been expecting the government to sign a negotiated agreement.

No comment from De Beers' negotiating partner, diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), was available, although a senior company official said on Monday he expected the agreement to be signed in January.
